item.title: [Lanka Talks] Why Sri Lanka's plantation future demands a new investment outlook
item.description: A tea bush planted today may take five years to produce a crop, a decade to generate meaningful returns and more than 20 years to repay the investment. Yet Sri Lanka's regional plantation companies have only 19 years remaining on their leases. This is the contradiction at the heart of the country's plantation economy: an industry whose future depends on long-term investment is operating within a policy framework that makes such investment increasingly difficult to justify.
